```{julia}
using Statistics, StatsBase, GLM, FixedEffectModels
using CategoricalArrays, LinearAlgebra
using RegressionTables
using KernelDensity, Loess
using RDatasets, Random, Printf
using Optim, Distributions, SpecialFunctions, HypothesisTests

using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end
```

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

"""
    rmcoll_stata(df, vars; tol=1e-9, quiet=false) -> Vector{Symbol}

Stata-style `_rmcoll`: scan `vars` in order and drop any variable whose
multiple-correlation R² with the previously kept set exceeds `1 − tol`.
Stata's default tolerance is `1e-9`. Returns the surviving varlist; with
`quiet=false` (the default) prints `note: <var> omitted because of
collinearity` for each dropped variable, matching Stata's wording.
"""
function rmcoll_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars;
                     tol::Float64 = 1e-9, quiet::Bool = false)
    varlist = Symbol.(vars)
    sub = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, varlist])
    M   = hcat([Float64.(collect(sub[!, v])) for v in varlist]...)
    n   = size(M, 1)
    keep = trues(length(varlist))
    keep[1] = true
    for j in 2:length(varlist)
        Xj = M[:, findall(keep[1:j-1])]
        yj = M[:, j]
        # Regression with intercept: residual SS / total SS
        Xa = hcat(ones(n), Xj)
        β  = Xa \ yj
        ŷ  = Xa * β
        rss = sum((yj .- ŷ).^2)
        tss = sum((yj .- Statistics.mean(yj)).^2)
        r2  = tss > 0 ? 1 - rss / tss : 1.0
        if 1 - r2 < tol
            keep[j] = false
            quiet || println("note: ", varlist[j], " omitted because of collinearity")
        end
    end
    return varlist[keep]
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

function poisson_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:robust, level::Float64=0.95,
                       quiet::Bool=false,
                       layout::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                       header_style::Symbol=:poisson,
                       cluster_var=nothing)
    # Drop missing for variables in formula (and the cluster var, if any)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed :
                                       vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Fit Poisson GLM
    m = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β  = GLM.coef(m)
    cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m))
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    μ  = GLM.predict(m)
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)
    k  = size(Xm, 2)

    # If `cluster_var` is given, force vce → :cluster regardless of caller's
    # choice (Stata's `vce(cluster <var>)` syntax), and capture cluster count.
    n_clusters = 0
    if cluster_var !== nothing
        vce = :cluster
        n_clusters = length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
    end

    # SE: robust sandwich (default) / cluster-robust (CR1) / OIM.
    # Stata's `vce(robust)` uses n/(n-1) finite-sample correction.
    # `vce(cluster G)` uses (G/(G-1))·(n-1)/(n-k) and aggregates scores by
    # cluster: B = Σ_g (X_g'(y_g − μ_g)) (X_g'(y_g − μ_g))'.
    if vce == :robust
        H = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        meat = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal((yv .- μ).^2) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        V = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (n / (n - 1))
    elseif vce == :cluster
        cluster_var === nothing &&
            error("vce = :cluster requires `cluster_var = :varname`")
        cl = dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]
        u  = (yv .- μ) .* Xm                # n×k per-obs scores X_i·(y_i−μ_i)
        # Aggregate scores by cluster, then meat = Σ_g s_g s_g'.
        meat = zeros(k, k)
        for g in unique(cl)
            sg = vec(sum(u[cl .== g, :], dims = 1))
            meat .+= sg * sg'
        end
        H    = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        G    = n_clusters
        # Stata's `poisson, vce(cluster)` uses ONLY the G/(G−1) cluster
        # adjustment — no extra (n−1)/(n−k) factor (that one is OLS-style).
        V    = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (G / (G - 1))
    else
        V = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    # Slopes (excluding intercept) — used for both Wald and LR
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), [intercept_idx])
    Wald = NaN; Wald_p = NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_slope = β[slope_idx]
        V_slope = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald = β_slope' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_slope) * β_slope
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)
    end

    # Log pseudolikelihood and Pseudo R² (McFadden's-like: 1 - LL/LL_null)
    ll  = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    # Null model: intercept only
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null

    # LR chi² on slopes — Stata's default `poisson` reports `LR chi2(k)`;
    # `vce(robust|cluster)` switches it to `Wald chi2(k)` (LR is invalid
    # under misspecification of the likelihood).
    LR_chi2 = !isempty(slope_idx) ? 2 * (ll - ll_null) : NaN
    LR_p    = !isempty(slope_idx) ?
              1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR_chi2) :
              NaN

    # Stata %9.0g formatter — sign-aware width cap (cap=9 except cap=10 for
    # negative |x|<1, where leading-zero strip saves a char). Without this
    # asymmetry, negative |x|<1 values would lose a digit vs Stata's output.
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1
            push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3
        end
        return (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Skip the entire Stata-style printout when quiet=true (mirrors Stata's
    # `quietly poisson ...`). Useful for chapter chunks that just need β/V/X
    # for downstream margins/dydx/etc. and don't want to repeat the table.
    if !quiet
    # Print Stata-style header. Two layouts:
    #   :poisson — Stata's `poisson` command output. Top-left says "Poisson
    #              regression", and the right column lists Number of obs /
    #              Wald chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Pseudo R2 over four lines,
    #              with "Log pseudolikelihood = …" on the last line at left.
    #   :ml      — Stata's `ml maximize` output. No "Poisson regression"
    #              header; the right column lists Number of obs / Wald
    #              chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 over three lines, with "Log
    #              [pseudo]likelihood = …" on the third line at left, and
    #              no Pseudo R2 row.
    println()
    if header_style == :ml
        # Stata `ml maximize` right-block format: 13-char left-padded label,
        # " = ", then a value field whose width is the max of the three
        # value strings plus 1 (so the longest value sits 1 space after `=`,
        # shorter ones are right-aligned). The whole right block is positioned
        # flush right at col 78 by adjusting the leading whitespace.
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        wstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", Wald) : ""
        pstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Wald_p) : ""
        vw   = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr))
        rblock = 13 + 3 + vw
        lead   = max(0, 78 - rblock)
        ws     = " " ^ lead
        println(ws, rpad("Number of obs", 13), " = ", lpad(nstr, vw))
        if isfinite(Wald)
            println(ws, rpad("Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", 13),
                    " = ", lpad(wstr, vw))
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str   = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.3f", ll_label, ll)
        println(rpad(ll_str, lead), rpad("Prob > chi2", 13), " = ", lpad(pstr, vw))
    else
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Poisson regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        # `LR chi2` for OIM (default), `Wald chi2` for robust/cluster.
        chi2_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Wald" : "LR"
        chi2_val   = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald   : LR_chi2
        chi2_p     = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald_p : LR_p
        if isfinite(chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                           "$chi2_label chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", chi2_p)
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ?
                   "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.5f", ll_label, ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad_h  = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad_h, r2_str)
    end
    println()

    # Cluster sub-note (Stata: "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in <var>)"),
    # right-aligned at col 78.
    if vce == :cluster
        cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Std. err. adjusted for %d clusters in %s)",
                                 n_clusters, cluster_var)
        println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
    end

    # Coefficient table. Stata uses lowercase "std. err." under the "Robust"
    # subheader for `vce(robust)` / `vce(cluster …)` and capital "Std. err."
    # for the default OIM.
    println("-"^78)
    if vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        println("             |               Robust")
    end
    se_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
    Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(formula.lhs), se_label)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

    # `_print_row(label, idx)` renders a single row in Stata's standard
    # 7-column layout. `_lookup(key)` finds the GLM-order index from a
    # coefname or returns the index directly.
    _print_row(label, idx) = Printf.@printf(
        "%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
        label, g9(β[idx]; w=10), g9(se[idx]; w=9),
        Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[idx]),
        Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[idx]),
        g9(ci_lo[idx]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[idx]; w=10))
    _lookup(key) = key isa Integer ? Int(key) :
        (let i = findfirst(==(string(key)), cn)
            i === nothing && error("'$(key)' not found in coefnames=$(cn)")
            i
        end)

    if layout === nothing
        # Default layout: slopes (in formula order) first, then _cons.
        for i in slope_idx
            _print_row(cn[i], i)
        end
        intercept_idx !== nothing && _print_row("_cons", intercept_idx)
    else
        # Custom layout. Each entry is one of:
        #   :blank                       → empty separator row "             |"
        #   String  => key                → simple row, label = String
        #   Vector{String} => key         → multi-line interaction block: all
        #                                    but the last element are header
        #                                    lines (printed as `<line>|`),
        #                                    last element is the row label.
        # `key` can be a coefname (matched against the GLM-order coefnames)
        # or a 1-based integer index into β.
        for entry in layout
            if entry === :blank
                println("             |")
            elseif entry isa Pair
                lab, key = entry.first, entry.second
                # `label => :omitted` — Stata-style "(omitted)" row for a
                # variable that was dropped due to collinearity. Prints
                # "        label |          0  (omitted)" with no key lookup.
                if key === :omitted
                    Printf.@printf("%12s |          0  (omitted)\n", string(lab))
                    continue
                end
                idx = _lookup(key)
                if lab isa AbstractVector
                    for h in lab[1:end-1]
                        println(h, "|")
                    end
                    _print_row(string(lab[end]), idx)
                else
                    _print_row(string(lab), idx)
                end
            else
                error("Unsupported layout entry: $entry (use :blank or label=>key)")
            end
        end
    end
    println("-"^78)
    end  # if !quiet

    # Return values in *Stata's display order*: slopes first, then _cons.
    # That way the margins / nlcom / lincom / dydx helpers can be called
    # directly on these without any reordering, and the constant always
    # sits at the end of β (matching the convention used throughout the
    # downstream chapter chunks).
    if intercept_idx === nothing
        ord = collect(slope_idx)
        cn_ord = cn[ord]
    else
        ord = vcat(collect(slope_idx), [intercept_idx])
        cn_ord = vcat(cn[slope_idx], "_cons")
    end
    β_ord  = β[ord]
    se_ord = se[ord]
    V_ord  = V[ord, ord]
    X_ord  = Xm[:, ord]   # last column = ones (the constant)

    return (; model=m, df=dfc, formula,
              β=β_ord, se=se_ord, V=V_ord, X=X_ord,
              coefnames=cn_ord,
              Wald, Wald_p, ll, pseudo_r2, n, k,
              # Originals (GLM order) preserved for any code that needs them:
              β_glm=β, V_glm=V, X_glm=Xm, coefnames_glm=cn)
end

function poisson_nll(β, X, y)
    η = X * β
    μ = exp.(η)
    -sum(.-μ .+ y .* η .- SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y .+ 1))
end
```

### 11.2.3 Poisson NR example using native Julia matrix algebra

#### Core Julia code for Poisson NR iterations

```{julia}
# Pseudocode for Newton-Raphson Poisson MLE
# (X is n×k, y is n×1, b is k×1; tolerance = 1e-16)
#
#   b   = zeros(k);  iter = 0;  cha = 1
#   while cha > 1e-16
#       μ    = exp.(X * b)
#       grad = X' * (y .- μ)            # k×1 score
#       hes  = X' * Diagonal(μ) * X     # k×k negative Hessian
#       bold = b
#       b    = bold + cholesky(Symmetric(hes)) \ grad
#       cha  = sum((bold .- b).^2) / sum(bold.^2)
#       iter += 1
#   end
```

#### Complete Julia code for Poisson NR iterations


```{julia}
# Verbose Poisson MLE via raw Newton–Raphson, showing parameter vector and
# gradient at every iteration — for comparison with the standard fit above.
# (Stata: poisson docvis private chronic female income, log trace gradient
#         iterate(100) tol(1e-4) ltol(0) robust)
#
# Score   ∇ℓ(β) = X'(y − μ),    Hessian H(β) = −X' diag(μ) X.
# Update  β_{k+1} = β_k + (X' diag(μ) X)⁻¹ · X'(y − μ).
# Stops when max |Δβ_j| / (|β_j| + ε) < 1e-4 (Stata's tol(...)).

dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
y_v = Float64.(dfc.docvis)
X_v = hcat(Float64.(dfc.private), Float64.(dfc.chronic),
           Float64.(dfc.female),  Float64.(dfc.income),
           ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfc)))
varnames_v = ["private", "chronic", "female", "income", "_cons"]
n_v, k_v   = size(X_v)
depvar_v   = "docvis"
ll_const   = sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y_v .+ 1))

# Stata-style %9.0g for one number (sign-aware cap so negative |x|<1 keeps
# 7 sig digs after the leading-zero strip).
_g = function (x; sig::Int=7)
    sig_use = sig
    s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
    while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
        sig_use -= 1
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    end
    0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    s
end

function _print_iter(iter, β, ll, g)
    println("-"^81)
    Printf.@printf("Iteration %d:\n", iter)
    println("Parameter vector:")
    print("  ")
    for _ in 1:k_v
        Printf.@printf("%11s", "$(depvar_v):")
    end
    println()
    print("  ")
    for nm in varnames_v
        Printf.@printf("%11s", nm)
    end
    println()
    print("r1")
    for j in 1:k_v
        Printf.@printf("%11s", _g(β[j]))
    end
    println()
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%48sLog pseudolikelihood = %s\n", "", _g(ll))
    Printf.@printf("Gradient vector (length = %s):\n", _g(sqrt(sum(g.^2))))
    print("  ")
    for _ in 1:k_v
        Printf.@printf("%11s", "$(depvar_v):")
    end
    println()
    print("  ")
    for nm in varnames_v
        Printf.@printf("%11s", nm)
    end
    println()
    print("r1")
    for j in 1:k_v
        Printf.@printf("%11s", _g(g[j]))
    end
    println()
end

# Newton–Raphson loop
β_nr = zeros(k_v)
for iter in 0:100
    μ_nr = exp.(X_v * β_nr)
    ll_nr = sum(y_v .* log.(μ_nr) .- μ_nr) - ll_const
    g_nr  = X_v' * (y_v .- μ_nr)
    _print_iter(iter, β_nr, ll_nr, g_nr)

    H_nr = X_v' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ_nr) * X_v
    Δ    = H_nr \ g_nr
    if maximum(abs.(Δ) ./ (abs.(β_nr) .+ 1e-10)) < 1e-4
        β_nr .+= Δ
        break
    end
    β_nr .+= Δ
end
println("-"^81)

# Print the final regression table in Stata's standard layout
poisson_stata(dfc,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :robust);
```

```{julia}
#=
* Poisson ML program lfpois to be called by command ml method lf
program lfpois
  version 11
  args lnf theta1                  // theta1=x'b, lnf=ln(y)
  tempvar lnyfact mu
  local y "$ML_y1"                 // Define y so program more readable
  generate double `lnyfact' = lnfactorial(`y')
  generate double `mu'      = exp(`theta1')
  quietly replace `lnf'     = -`mu' + `y'*`theta1' - `lnyfact'
end
=#
# Optim with NewtonTrustRegion for Poisson MLE — robust SEs separately
β0 = zeros(k11)
res_pois = _optimize_compat(β -> poisson_nll(β, X11, y11), β0,
                          Optim.LBFGS(); autodiff = :forward)
println(res_pois)
β_pois = Optim.minimizer(res_pois)
println("Coefficients: ", round.(β_pois, digits = 6))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Command ml model including defining y and x, plus ml check
ml model lf lfpois (docvis = private chronic female income), vce(robust)
ml check
=#
# Compute robust SE manually (sandwich)
μ_p = exp.(X11 * β_pois)
H   = X11' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ_p) * X11
S   = X11' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal((y11 .- μ_p).^2) * X11
V_p = try
        LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H))) * S *
              LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
    catch
        LinearAlgebra.pinv(H) * S * LinearAlgebra.pinv(H)
    end *
      (n11 / (n11 - k11))
se_p = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_p))
println("\n— Optim.jl Poisson MLE with robust SE —")
for i in 1:k11
    @printf("%-10s %12.6f  se=%10.6f\n", xnms11[i], β_pois[i], se_p[i])
end
```

```{julia}
#=
* Search for better starting values
ml search
=#
# Compute log-likelihood at optimum
@printf("Log-likelihood = %.4f\n", -Optim.minimum(res_pois))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Compute the estimator
ml maximize 
=#
# Poisson MLE via a user-supplied log-likelihood — the Julia analogue of
# Stata's `ml model lf lfpois ...; ml check; ml search; ml maximize`.
# The "lfpois evaluator" is the closure `lfpois(β)` below; it returns the
# total log-likelihood (Optim minimizes the negative).
# (Stata: program lfpois; args lnf theta1; ...;
#         ml model lf lfpois (docvis = private chronic female income), vce(robust);
#         ml check; ml search; ml maximize)

dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
y_v = Float64.(dfc.docvis)
X_v = hcat(Float64.(dfc.private), Float64.(dfc.chronic),
           Float64.(dfc.female),  Float64.(dfc.income),
           ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfc)))
n_v, k_v = size(X_v)
ll_const = sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y_v .+ 1))

# Stata's `lfpois` evaluator written as a single Julia function:
#     ln f_i(β) = -μ_i + y_i · θ_i - ln(y_i!)   where  θ_i = x_i'β,  μ_i = exp(θ_i)
# Returned as the SUM (total log-likelihood); Optim feeds the negative.
function lfpois(β)
    θ = X_v * β
    μ = exp.(θ)
    return sum(y_v .* θ .- μ) - ll_const
end

# Newton-Raphson, mirroring `ml maximize`'s iteration log
println("Initial:      Log pseudolikelihood = ",
        Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", lfpois(zeros(k_v))))
β_ml = zeros(k_v)
for iter in 0:100
    Printf.@printf("Iteration %d:  Log pseudolikelihood = %.3f\n",
                   iter, lfpois(β_ml))
    μ_it = exp.(X_v * β_ml)
    g_it = X_v' * (y_v .- μ_it)
    H_it = X_v' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ_it) * X_v
    Δ    = H_it \ g_it
    if maximum(abs.(Δ) ./ (abs.(β_ml) .+ 1e-10)) < 1e-4
        β_ml .+= Δ
        break
    end
    β_ml .+= Δ
end
println()

# `ml maximize, vce(robust)` produces the regression table — same format
# as `poisson_stata`, since the converged β is identical.
poisson_stata(dfc,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :robust);
```

### 11.4.4 Negative binomial example: Two-index model

```{julia}
#=
* Negbin ML program lfnb to be called by command ml method lf
program lfnb
  version 11
  args lnf theta1 a               // theta1=x'b, a=alpha, lnf=ln(y)
  tempvar mu
  local y $ML_y1                  // Define y so program more readable
  generate double `mu'  = exp(`theta1')
  quietly replace `lnf' = lngamma(`y'+(1/`a')) - lngamma((1/`a'))  ///
               -  lnfactorial(`y') - (`y'+(1/`a'))*ln(1+`a'*`mu')  ///
               + `y'*ln(`a') + `y'*ln(`mu') 
end
=#
# Negative binomial MLE: parameters are (β, α). Use log(α) for unconstrained.
function negbin_nll(params, X, y)
    p = size(X, 2)
    β = params[1:p]
    α = exp(params[p + 1])
    η = X * β
    μ = exp.(η)
    inv_α = 1 / α
    ll = sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y .+ inv_α) .-
             SpecialFunctions.loggamma(inv_α) .-
             SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y .+ 1) .-
             (y .+ inv_α) .* log.(1 .+ α .* μ) .+
             y .* log(α) .+ y .* η)
    return -ll
end

res_nb = _optimize_compat(params -> negbin_nll(params, X11, y11),
                        vcat(β_pois, log(1.0)),
                        Optim.LBFGS(); autodiff = :forward)
β_nb = Optim.minimizer(res_nb)
α_nb = exp(β_nb[end])
println("\n— NegBin MLE coefficients —")
for i in 1:k11
    @printf("%-10s %12.6f\n", xnms11[i], β_nb[i])
end
@printf("alpha     = %.6f\n", α_nb)
@printf("logL      = %.4f\n", -Optim.minimum(res_nb))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Command lf implemented for negative binomial MLE
ml model lf lfnb (docvis = private chronic female income) ()
ml maximize, nolog
=#
# Negative-binomial MLE via a user-supplied two-equation log-likelihood,
# matching Stata's `ml model lf lfnb (docvis = private chronic female income) ()`
# eq1 = β (linear index for μ);  eq2 = α (NB2 dispersion, fitted DIRECTLY,
# not log α — same as Stata's lfnb).
# (Stata: program lfnb; args lnf theta1 a; ...;
#         ml model lf lfnb (docvis = ...) (); ml maximize, nolog)

dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
y_v = Float64.(dfc.docvis)
X_v = hcat(Float64.(dfc.private), Float64.(dfc.chronic),
           Float64.(dfc.female),  Float64.(dfc.income),
           ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfc)))
n_v, kβ_v = size(X_v)
varnames_v = ["private", "chronic", "female", "income", "_cons"]

# Stata's lfnb evaluator written as a single Julia function (NB2, α direct):
#   ln f_i = lnΓ(y+1/α) − lnΓ(1/α) − lnΓ(y+1)
#            − (y+1/α)·ln(1+α·μ) + y·ln(α) + y·ln(μ),    μ = exp(x'β)
function lfnb_total(p)
    β = p[1:kβ_v]; α = p[end]
    α <= 0 && return -1e10
    μ = exp.(X_v * β)
    invα = 1 / α
    return sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y_v .+ invα)
              .- SpecialFunctions.loggamma(invα)
              .- SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y_v .+ 1)
              .- (y_v .+ invα) .* log.(1 .+ α .* μ)
              .+ y_v .* log(α)
              .+ y_v .* log.(μ))
end

# Maximize via L-BFGS with autodiff (`ml maximize`'s default is BHHH-like;
# either converges to the same MLE).
const FD = ForwardDiff   # ForwardDiff is now a direct dep (Project.toml); Optim no longer vendors it accessibly
p0   = vcat(zeros(kβ_v), 1.0)                 # β = 0, α = 1
res  = _optimize_compat(p -> -lfnb_total(p), p0, Optim.LBFGS();
                      autodiff = :forward)
p_ml = Optim.minimizer(res)
β_ml = p_ml[1:kβ_v]; α_ml = p_ml[end]
ll_max = -Optim.minimum(res)

# OIM standard errors from inverse Hessian of the negative log-likelihood
H_ml = FD.hessian(p -> -lfnb_total(p), p_ml)
V_ml = LinearAlgebra.inv(H_ml)
se_ml = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_ml))
z_ml  = p_ml ./ se_ml
pv_ml = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_ml)))
crit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 0.975)
lo_ml = p_ml .- crit .* se_ml
hi_ml = p_ml .+ crit .* se_ml

# Wald chi² on β slopes (excluding α and the eq1 intercept)
slope_idx = 1:4
W = β_ml[slope_idx]' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_ml[slope_idx, slope_idx]) * β_ml[slope_idx]
W_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), W)

# Stata-style table (two equations, eq1 / eq2 sub-headers)
g9 = function (x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
    sig_use = sig
    s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
    while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
        sig_use -= 1
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    end
    0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    lpad(s, w_)
end
commafmt(num::Integer) = begin
    s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
    while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
    (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
end
function row(label, idx)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                   label, g9(p_ml[idx]; w_=10), g9(se_ml[idx]; w_=9),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_ml[idx]),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pv_ml[idx]),
                   g9(lo_ml[idx]; w_=9), g9(hi_ml[idx]; w_=10))
end

println()
Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n", "", "Number of obs", commafmt(n_v))
Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "", "Wald chi2(4)", W)
Printf.@printf("Log likelihood = %.4f%23s%-13s = %6.4f\n",
               ll_max, "", "Prob > chi2", W_p)
println()
println("-"^78)
Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
               "docvis")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "eq1")
for i in 1:5
    row(varnames_v[i], i)
end
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "eq2")
row("_cons", 6)
println("-"^78)
```

### 11.4.5 NLS example: Nonlikelihood model

```{julia}
#=
* NLS program lfnls to be called by command ml method lf
program lfnls
  version 11
  args lnf theta1                 // theta1=x'b, lnf=squared residual
  local y "$ML_y1"                // Define y so program more readable
  quietly replace `lnf' = -(`y'-exp(`theta1'))^2
end
=#
# NLS via the lf "pseudo-likelihood" trick — Stata's `ml model lf lfnls`
# treats lnf = -(y − exp(x'β))² as a per-observation log-likelihood, so
# maximizing Σ lnf is the same as minimizing the SSR of the Poisson mean
# function. Robust SE is the BHHH-style sandwich on the SSR's score.
# (Stata: program lfnls; args lnf theta1; replace lnf = -(y - exp(theta1))^2;
#         ml model lf lfnls (docvis = ...), vce(robust); ml maximize)

dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
y_v = Float64.(dfc.docvis)
X_v = hcat(Float64.(dfc.private), Float64.(dfc.chronic),
           Float64.(dfc.female),  Float64.(dfc.income),
           ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfc)))
n_v, k_v = size(X_v)
varnames_v = ["private", "chronic", "female", "income", "_cons"]

# Stata's lfnls evaluator: total "pseudo-log-lik" is just −SSR
function lfnls_total(β)
    μ = exp.(X_v * β)
    return -sum((y_v .- μ).^2)
end

# Maximize via L-BFGS (mirrors Stata's `ml maximize`)
res    = _optimize_compat(β -> -lfnls_total(β), zeros(k_v), Optim.LBFGS(),
                        Optim.Options(g_tol = 1e-10, iterations = 500);
                        autodiff = :forward)
β_nls  = Optim.minimizer(res)
ll_max = lfnls_total(β_nls)              # = −SSR (Stata's "Log pseudolikelihood")

# Robust sandwich. Score s_i(β) = ∂lnf_i/∂β = 2 u_i μ_i x_i,  u_i = y_i − μ_i.
# OPG:    Σ s_i s_i' = 4 X' diag(μ²·u²) X.
# Hessian: H_i = ∂²lnf_i/∂β∂β' = 2 μ_i (y_i − 2μ_i) x_i x_i', so
#         −H = 2 X' diag(μ·(2μ − y)) X.
# V_robust = (−H)⁻¹ · OPG · (−H)⁻¹ · n/(n−1)   ← Stata's small-sample correction
μ_nls = exp.(X_v * β_nls)
u_nls = y_v .- μ_nls
negH  = 2 * (X_v' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ_nls .* (2 .* μ_nls .- y_v)) * X_v)
OPG   = 4 * (X_v' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ_nls.^2 .* u_nls.^2) * X_v)
V_nls = LinearAlgebra.inv(negH) * OPG * LinearAlgebra.inv(negH) * (n_v / (n_v - 1))
se_nls = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_nls))
z_nls  = β_nls ./ se_nls
pv_nls = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_nls)))
crit   = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 0.975)
lo_nls = β_nls .- crit .* se_nls
hi_nls = β_nls .+ crit .* se_nls

# Wald χ² on β slopes (private, chronic, female, income — not _cons)
slope_idx_nls = 1:4
W_nls   = β_nls[slope_idx_nls]' *
          LinearAlgebra.inv(V_nls[slope_idx_nls, slope_idx_nls]) *
          β_nls[slope_idx_nls]
W_p_nls = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx_nls)), W_nls)

# Stata-style table  (single-equation, like `poisson_stata` with vce(robust))
g9 = function (x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
    sig_use = sig
    s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
    while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
        sig_use -= 1
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    end
    0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    lpad(s, w_)
end
commafmt(num::Integer) = begin
    s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
    while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
    (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
end
function row(label, idx)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                   label, g9(β_nls[idx]; w_=10), g9(se_nls[idx]; w_=9),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_nls[idx]),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pv_nls[idx]),
                   g9(lo_nls[idx]; w_=9), g9(hi_nls[idx]; w_=10))
end

println()
Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n", "", "Number of obs", commafmt(n_v))
Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "", "Wald chi2(4)", W_nls)
Printf.@printf("Log pseudolikelihood = %.2f%19s%-13s = %6.4f\n",
               ll_max, "", "Prob > chi2", W_p_nls)
println()
println("-"^78)
println("             |               Robust")
Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
               "docvis")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
for i in 1:k_v
    row(varnames_v[i], i)
end
println("-"^78)
```

## 11.5 Checking the program

### 11.5.1 Program debugging

```{julia}
# High collinearity (extra ≈ income + tiny noise)
Random.seed!(10101)
df11.extra = df11.income .+ 0.001 .* rand(DataFrames.nrow(df11))
X11_e = hcat(X11, df11.extra)
@printf("Condition number = %.2e\n", LinearAlgebra.cond(X11_e))
```

```{julia}
# Near-perfect collinearity: `extra = income + tiny noise`. Stata's `ml` (and
# its other estimators) detect near-singularity in the design matrix via
# `_rmcoll` and drop the offending column, reporting it as "(omitted)".
# (Stata: gen extra = income + 0.001*runiform();
#         ml model lf lfpois (docvis = private chronic female income extra),
#         vce(robust); ml maximize)

dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
Random.seed!(10101)
dfc.extra = dfc.income .+ 0.001 .* rand(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))

# Stata `_rmcoll`-style collinearity check: scan regressors in the user-given
# order and flag any column whose absolute correlation with an earlier kept
# column exceeds 1 - 1e-5 (matches Stata's default behaviour of dropping the
# *later* variable).
X_full        = hcat(Float64.(dfc.private), Float64.(dfc.chronic),
                     Float64.(dfc.female),  Float64.(dfc.income),
                     Float64.(dfc.extra))
varnames_full = ["private", "chronic", "female", "income", "extra"]
keep          = trues(size(X_full, 2))
for j in 2:size(X_full, 2), i in 1:(j-1)
    keep[i] && abs(Statistics.cor(X_full[:, i], X_full[:, j])) > 1 - 1e-5 &&
        (keep[j] = false; break)
end
omitted_names = varnames_full[.!keep]
println("Collinearity check: dropping ", omitted_names)

# Refit Poisson on the surviving regressors using `poisson_stata`'s `layout`
# keyword to inject the "extra | 0 (omitted)" row in Stata's exact spot.
poisson_stata(dfc,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :robust,
    layout = [
        "private" => "private",
        "chronic" => "chronic",
        "female"  => "female",
        "income"  => "income",
        "extra"   => :omitted,
        "_cons"   => "(Intercept)",
    ]);
```

### 11.5.2 Getting the program to run

```{julia}
#=
*quietly replace `lnf' = `mu' + `y'*ln(`mu') - `lnyfact'
*mlmaximize
=#
# Buggy lfpois — sign on the μ term flipped from − to +. Stata's source
# commented this out (it would blow up), but it's a useful demo: the
# resulting "log-likelihood" is unbounded above, so the optimizer diverges
# (β → +∞ pushes μ → ∞, and the loss → +∞ along with it).
# (Stata: replace lnf = mu + y*ln(mu) - lnyfact;  ml maximize)

dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
y_v = Float64.(dfc.docvis)
X_v = hcat(Float64.(dfc.private), Float64.(dfc.chronic),
           Float64.(dfc.female),  Float64.(dfc.income),
           ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfc)))
n_v, k_v = size(X_v)
ll_const = sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y_v .+ 1))

# WRONG sign on μ (correct version subtracts μ)
function lfpois_buggy(β)
    θ = X_v * β
    μ = exp.(θ)
    return sum(μ .+ y_v .* θ) - ll_const   # NOTE: `+ μ` is the bug
end

# Show the loss climbing toward +∞ as β walks in the gradient direction.
# Score: ∂lnf_i/∂β = (μ_i + y_i) · x_i   →   always pulls β to +∞.
println("Buggy log-pseudolikelihood at β = 0:        ",
        Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", lfpois_buggy(zeros(k_v))))
for step in [0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5]
    β_walk = step .* (X_v' * (y_v .+ exp.(X_v * zeros(k_v)))) ./ n_v
    Printf.@printf("β scaled by step=%.2f          → lnf = %.3f\n",
                   step, lfpois_buggy(β_walk))
end

# Try Optim and watch it fail (the optimizer minimizes -lfnp_buggy, which
# is unbounded BELOW, so it walks β to +∞ and trips a numerical overflow).
res = try
    _optimize_compat(β -> -lfpois_buggy(β), zeros(k_v), Optim.LBFGS(),
                   Optim.Options(iterations = 50, g_tol = 1e-6);
                   autodiff = :forward)
catch e
    e
end
println("\nOptim result: ", res isa Exception ? "ERROR — $(typeof(res))" :
        (Optim.converged(res) ? "(spuriously) converged" : "did not converge"))
res isa Optim.OptimizationResults && Printf.@printf(
    "  iterations: %d   final ‘lnf’: %.3e   max|β|: %.3e\n",
    Optim.iterations(res), -Optim.minimum(res),
    maximum(abs.(Optim.minimizer(res))))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Detect multicollinearity using _rmcoll
_rmcoll income extra 
_rmcoll income extra2
=#
# Variance Inflation Factors (VIF) — manual computation
function vif(X, names)
    p = size(X, 2)
    vifs = zeros(p)
    for j in 1:p
        y_j = X[:, j]
        Xj  = X[:, setdiff(1:p, j)]
        β_j = (Xj' * Xj) \ (Xj' * y_j)
        ŷ_j = Xj * β_j
        r2  = 1 - sum((y_j .- ŷ_j).^2) / sum((y_j .- Statistics.mean(y_j)).^2)
        vifs[j] = 1 / (1 - r2)
    end
    println("─" ^ 30)
    @printf("%-10s %12s\n", "Variable", "VIF")
    println("─" ^ 30)
    for i in 1:p
        @printf("%-10s %12.2f\n", names[i], vifs[i])
    end
    println("─" ^ 30)
    return vifs
end

println("VIFs with 'extra' (very collinear):")
vif(hcat(df11.income, df11.extra), ["income", "extra"])
println()
println("VIFs with 'extra2' (less collinear):")
vif(hcat(df11.income, df11.extra2), ["income", "extra2"])
```

```{julia}
# High-but-not-perfect collinearity: `extra2 = income + 0.01·U(0,1)` is correlated
# with `income` at ≈1 − 5·10⁻⁹, well below Stata's `_rmcoll` tolerance of 1 − 10⁻⁵.
# Stata KEEPS both regressors and reports huge offsetting coefficients with very
# wide SEs — the sandwich variance still exists because the Hessian is nonsingular,
# only ill-conditioned. (Contrast with §11.5.1, where 0.001·U(0,1) noise is tight
# enough that `_rmcoll` drops `extra` as "(omitted)".)
# (Stata: gen extra2 = income + 0.01*runiform();
#         ml model lf lfpois (docvis = private chronic female income extra2),
#         vce(robust); ml maximize, nolog)

dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
Random.seed!(10101)
dfc.extra2 = dfc.income .+ 0.01 .* rand(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))

# Verify the correlation is below Stata's drop threshold (so no column is omitted)
@printf("cor(income, extra2) = %.10f   |1 − cor| = %.2e   (Stata threshold ≈ 1e-5)\n",
        Statistics.cor(dfc.income, dfc.extra2),
        1 - abs(Statistics.cor(dfc.income, dfc.extra2)))

# Fit on all five regressors via `poisson_stata` with vce(robust). The optimum
# sits on a near-flat ridge: β_income ≈ −β_extra2 with SEs of the same order
# as the point estimates and z-stats well below 2 — the data identify only
# their sum, not the two coefficients separately.
#
# The exact magnitude of β_income depends on the realised noise vector. The
# book reports β_income ≈ 12.23 (log L ≈ −18492.27); Julia here lands on
# β_income ≈ 6.92 (log L ≈ −18500.09). The difference is the RNG: Stata uses
# 64-bit Mersenne Twister (MT64) with a 312-element state, while Julia's
# default is `Xoshiro256++` and `MersenneTwister` is the 32-bit MT19937 variant
# — none reproduce Stata's `runiform()` sequence from the same seed value.
# Qualitatively the finding is identical: huge offsetting coefs, both kept by
# the optimiser rather than dropped, with very wide SEs.
poisson_stata(dfc,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income + extra2);
    vce = :robust);
```

```{julia}
# Stata's `_rmcoll` flags variables whose multiple-correlation R² with the
# previously kept variables exceeds 1 − tol (default tol = 1e-9). With
# 0.001·U(0,1) noise, 1 − R²(income, extra) ≈ 1e-10 < 1e-9 → `extra` is
# dropped. With 0.01·U(0,1) noise, 1 − R²(income, extra2) ≈ 1e-8 > 1e-9 →
# both kept (exactly why §11.5.2's `ml maximize` did not omit `extra2`).

dfc_rm = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
Random.seed!(10101)
dfc_rm.extra  = dfc_rm.income .+ 0.001 .* rand(DataFrames.nrow(dfc_rm))
Random.seed!(10101)
dfc_rm.extra2 = dfc_rm.income .+ 0.01  .* rand(DataFrames.nrow(dfc_rm))

println(". _rmcoll income extra")
kept_e  = rmcoll_stata(dfc_rm, [:income, :extra])
println("  kept: ", kept_e)

println("\n. _rmcoll income extra2")
kept_e2 = rmcoll_stata(dfc_rm, [:income, :extra2])
println("  kept: ", kept_e2)
```

### 11.5.7 Checking standard-error estimation

```{julia}
#=
* Program to generate dataset, obtain estimate, and return beta and SEs
program secheck, rclass
  version 11 
  drop _all 
  set obs 500 
  generate x = rnormal(0,0.5)
  generate mu = exp(2 + x)   
  generate y = rpoisson(mu)
  ml model lf lfpois (y = x)
  ml maximize
  return scalar b1 =_b[_cons]
  return scalar se1 = _se[_cons]
  return scalar b2 =_b[x]
  return scalar se2 = _se[x]
end
=#
# Monte-Carlo SE check. One replication generates 500 obs from the same
# Poisson DGP, fits Poisson MLE on (y = x), and returns (b_cons, se_cons,
# b_x, se_x) — matching Stata's `secheck` rclass program.
function secheck()
    x  = Distributions.rand(Distributions.Normal(0, 0.5), 500)
    μ  = exp.(2 .+ x)
    y  = [Distributions.rand(Distributions.Poisson(m)) for m in μ]
    df = DataFrames.DataFrame(y = y, x = x)
    m  = GLM.glm(GLM.@formula(y ~ x), df,
                 Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    i_c = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    i_x = findfirst(==("x"), cn)
    V   = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    return (bcons    = GLM.coef(m)[i_c], se_bcons = sqrt(V[i_c, i_c]),
            bx       = GLM.coef(m)[i_x], se_bx    = sqrt(V[i_x, i_x]))
end

# Stata: `set seed 10101; simulate secheck …, reps(2000); summarize`
Random.seed!(10101)
sims11 = [secheck() for _ in 1:2000]
df_sim = DataFrames.DataFrame(
    bcons    = [s.bcons    for s in sims11],
    se_bcons = [s.se_bcons for s in sims11],
    bx       = [s.bx       for s in sims11],
    se_bx    = [s.se_bx    for s in sims11])

summarize_stata(df_sim, [:bcons, :se_bcons, :bx, :se_bx]);
```

## 11.6 Custom evaluators (d0/d1/d2 equivalents)

### 11.6.1 Evaluator functions

In Julia, the evaluator pattern is: write a function that takes parameters and
data and returns the negative log-likelihood; for d1 also provide a gradient,
for d2 also provide a Hessian. `Optim.jl` accepts gradient/Hessian functions
or computes them via `autodiff = :forward`.

### 11.6.2 d0-style: only the log-likelihood

```{julia}
# Stata's `d0pois` evaluator computes the per-obs log-likelihood
#   lnf_i = −exp(θ_i) + y_i·θ_i − lnΓ(y_i + 1),  θ_i = x_iᵀβ
# and `mlsum` aggregates. The Julia analogue — defined in §11.4.3 — is
# `poisson_nll(β, X, y)`; minimising its negative via `Optim` is the d0
# method. Demonstrated here, then refit via `poisson_stata` so the printed
# table matches Stata's `ml maximize` exactly.

dfd = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income]])
y_d0 = Float64.(dfd.docvis)
X_d0 = hcat(Float64.(dfd.private), Float64.(dfd.chronic),
            Float64.(dfd.female),  Float64.(dfd.income),
            ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfd)))

# d0 demo: Optim with `poisson_nll` (no gradient supplied; autodiff handles it)
res_d0  = _optimize_compat(β -> poisson_nll(β, X_d0, y_d0),
                         zeros(size(X_d0, 2)),
                         Optim.LBFGS(); autodiff = :forward)
β_d0 = Optim.minimizer(res_d0)
@printf("d0 (Optim, autodiff)  log L = %.3f   β = %s\n",
        -Optim.minimum(res_d0), round.(β_d0, digits = 6))

# Same fit via the chunk-1 helper for the Stata-formatted table
poisson_stata(dfd,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :oim, header_style = :ml);
```

```{julia}
# Stata's d1 method augments d0 with an analytical gradient. For Poisson the
# score is ∂lnf_i/∂β = (y_i − exp(θ_i)) · x_i (equivalently ∑ Xᵀ(y − μ)). In
# Julia, supply both the NLL and an in-place gradient `g!(g, β)` to
# `Optim.optimize`. The sign is flipped because Optim minimises the negative
# log-likelihood.
function d1pois_grad!(g, β, X, y)
    g .= -X' * (y .- exp.(X * β))
end

res_d1 = _optimize_compat(β -> poisson_nll(β, X_d0, y_d0),
                        (g, β) -> d1pois_grad!(g, β, X_d0, y_d0),
                        zeros(size(X_d0, 2)),
                        Optim.LBFGS())
β_d1 = Optim.minimizer(res_d1)
@printf("d1 (Optim, analytical grad)  log L = %.3f   β = %s\n",
        -Optim.minimum(res_d1), round.(β_d1, digits = 6))
@printf("|β_d0 − β_d1|_∞ = %.3e (same MLE, different optimiser path)\n",
        maximum(abs.(β_d0 .- β_d1)))

# Stata-formatted table — identical to d0 since both methods converge to the
# same MLE.
poisson_stata(dfd,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :oim, header_style = :ml);
```

### 11.6.4 d1 with the robust estimate of the VCE

```{julia}
# `d1poisrob` is `d1pois` plus the per-observation score `g1 = y − exp(θ)`,
# which Stata's robust machinery uses to build the outer-product-of-gradients
# meat matrix B = ∑ g1_i g1_iᵀ x_i x_iᵀ. The sandwich is then A⁻¹ B A⁻¹ where
# A = ∑ exp(θ_i) x_i x_iᵀ is the OIM. The d1 fit is identical to §11.6.3 (same
# MLE); only the variance estimator changes. We refit via `poisson_stata` with
# `vce = :robust` so the helper computes the sandwich and prints the table in
# Stata's `ml maximize, vce(robust)` format ("Log pseudolikelihood", "Robust"
# subheader, lowercase "std. err.").
poisson_stata(dfd,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :robust, header_style = :ml);
```

### 11.6.5 d2-style: gradient + Hessian

```{julia}
# Method lf1: like d1 but the evaluator returns the *per-observation* log-lik
# and *per-observation* score (rather than aggregate quantities). Stata sums
# them internally; the per-obs scores are exactly what `vce(robust)` needs to
# build the OPG meat matrix B = ∑ g1_i g1_iᵀ x_i x_iᵀ.
#
# The Julia per-obs evaluator:
#   lnf_i(β)  = −exp(x_iᵀβ) + y_i · x_iᵀβ − lnΓ(y_i+1)
#   g1_i(β)  = (y_i − exp(x_iᵀβ)) · x_i
# (we don't need them as separate functions — Optim minimises the sum, and
# `poisson_stata` builds the sandwich from μ and (y−μ) directly).
#
# The lf1 fit is the same MLE as d0 / d1 / d1robust, and `vce(robust)` gives
# the same sandwich as d1poisrob. So the call is identical to §11.6.4.
poisson_stata(dfd,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :robust, header_style = :ml);
```

```{julia}
# Method d2: d1 plus the analytical Hessian. For Poisson:
#   ∇β lnL  = Xᵀ(y − μ)            (score, same as d1)
#   ∇²β lnL = −Xᵀ Diag(μ) X        (Hessian; negative-definite at the MLE)
# In Julia we supply both `g!(g, β)` and `H!(H, β)` to `Optim.optimize` and
# pick a second-order optimiser like `NewtonTrustRegion`. Since we minimise
# the *negative* log-likelihood, both gradient and Hessian flip sign:
#   ∇β  (−lnL) = −Xᵀ(y − μ)
#   ∇²β (−lnL) =  Xᵀ Diag(μ) X
function d2pois_grad!(g, β, X, y)
    g .= -X' * (y .- exp.(X * β))
end
function d2pois_hess!(H, β, X, y)
    μ = exp.(X * β)
    H .= X' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * X
end

res_d2 = _optimize_compat(β -> poisson_nll(β, X_d0, y_d0),
                        (g, β) -> d2pois_grad!(g, β, X_d0, y_d0),
                        (H, β) -> d2pois_hess!(H, β, X_d0, y_d0),
                        zeros(size(X_d0, 2)), Optim.NewtonTrustRegion())
β_d2 = Optim.minimizer(res_d2)
@printf("d2 (Optim, analytical grad + Hess)  log L = %.3f   β = %s\n",
        -Optim.minimum(res_d2), round.(β_d2, digits = 6))
@printf("|β_d0 − β_d2|_∞ = %.3e (same MLE; second-order method converges faster)\n",
        maximum(abs.(β_d0 .- β_d2)))

# Stata-formatted table — identical to d0 / d1 (same MLE, default OIM SEs).
poisson_stata(dfd,
    GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income);
    vce = :oim, header_style = :ml);
```

### 11.7.3 Poisson example

```{python}
%%stata
local y docvis
local xlist private chronic female income cons

mata: mata set matastrict off
* Evaluator function for Poisson MLE using optimize gf2 evaluator
mata 
  void poissonmle(todo, b, y, X, lndensity, g, H)
  {
    Xb = X*b'
    mu = exp(Xb)
    lndensity = -mu + y:*Xb - lnfactorial(y)
    if (todo == 0) return
    g = (y-mu):*X   
    if (todo == 1) return
    H = - cross(X, mu, X)
  }
end
```

#### The optimize() function for Poisson MLE 

```{julia}
#=
mata: mata drop poissonmle()
* Mata code to obtain Poisson MLE using command optimize
mata 
  void poissonmle(todo, b, y, X, lndensity, g, H)
  {
    Xb = X*b'
    mu = exp(Xb)
    lndensity = -mu + y:*Xb - lnfactorial(y)
    if (todo == 0) return
    g = (y-mu):*X   
    if (todo == 1) return
    H = - cross(X, mu, X)
  }
  st_view(y=., ., "`y'")  
  st_view(X=., ., tokens("`xlist'"))
  S = optimize_init()
  optimize_init_evaluator(S, &poissonmle())
  optimize_init_evaluatortype(S, "gf2")
  optimize_init_argument(S, 1, y)
  optimize_init_argument(S, 2, X)
  optimize_init_params(S, J(1,cols(X),0))
  b = optimize(S)  
  Vbrob = optimize_result_V_robust(S)
  serob = (sqrt(diagonal(Vbrob)))'
  b \ serob 
end
=#
# Mata's `optimize()` with a `gf2` evaluator wants per-obs log-density,
# gradient, and Hessian. Julia's `Optim.optimize` takes the aggregate NLL
# plus in-place `g!(g, β)` and `H!(H, β)`, then we build the robust sandwich
# manually (Mata's `optimize_result_V_robust`).

# Aggregate log-likelihood; sign-flipped for minimisation
function poisson_lnL(β, X, y)
    Xb = X * β
    μ  = exp.(Xb)
    -sum(y .* Xb .- μ .- SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(y .+ 1))
end
poisson_grad_mata!(g, β, X, y) = (g .= -X' * (y .- exp.(X * β)))
poisson_hess_mata!(H, β, X, y) =
    (H .= X' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(exp.(X * β)) * X)

res_mata = _optimize_compat(β -> poisson_lnL(β, X_d0, y_d0),
                          (g, β) -> poisson_grad_mata!(g, β, X_d0, y_d0),
                          (H, β) -> poisson_hess_mata!(H, β, X_d0, y_d0),
                          zeros(size(X_d0, 2)), Optim.NewtonTrustRegion())
b = Optim.minimizer(res_mata)

# Robust sandwich (the Mata `optimize_result_V_robust` analogue):
#   V = A⁻¹ B A⁻¹ · n/(n−1),  A = XᵀDiag(μ)X,  B = XᵀDiag((y−μ)²)X
n   = size(X_d0, 1)
μ   = exp.(X_d0 * b)
A   = X_d0' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * X_d0
B   = X_d0' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal((y_d0 .- μ).^2) * X_d0
Ainv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(A)))
Vbrob = Ainv * B * Ainv * (n / (n - 1))
serob = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(Vbrob))

# `b \ serob` in Mata stacks `b` on top of `serob` as a 2×k matrix
bs = vcat(b', serob')

# Mata-style matrix display: 4 cols per block, 10-digit numbers, leading
# zero stripped for |x| < 1 (matching Stata's `mata` shell output).
function _g10(x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 12 : 11
    for sig in 10:-1:1
        fmt = Printf.Format("%.$(sig)g")
        s   = Printf.format(fmt, x)
        s_strip = 0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        length(s_strip) <= cap && return s_strip
    end
    return Printf.@sprintf("%.1e", x)
end
function mata_matrix_print(M; cpb::Int = 4, w::Int = 15)
    nrows, ncols = size(M)
    for bs_col in 1:cpb:ncols
        be_col = min(bs_col + cpb - 1, ncols)
        Printf.@printf("    ")
        for c in bs_col:be_col; Printf.@printf("%*d", w, c); end
        println()
        bar = "+" * "-" ^ ((be_col - bs_col + 1) * w + 1) * "+"
        println("    ", bar)
        for r in 1:nrows
            Printf.@printf("  %d |", r)
            for c in bs_col:be_col
                Printf.@printf(" %*s", w - 1, _g10(M[r, c]))
            end
            println(" |")
        end
        println("    ", bar)
        be_col == ncols || println()
    end
end

println(":   Vbrob = optimize_result_V_robust(S)\n")
println(":   serob = (sqrt(diagonal(Vbrob)))'\n")
println(":   b \\ serob ")
mata_matrix_print(bs)
```

### 11.8.3 GMM via Optim.jl

```{julia}
# Poisson GMM with `firmsize` as an instrument for `private` (chronic, female,
# income, cons remain valid as both regressors and instruments). The moment
# function is the orthogonality condition Z'(y − exp(Xβ)) = 0; minimizing
#   Q(β) = h(β)' W h(β),  h = Z'(y − μ),  W = (Z'Z)⁻¹
# yields the GMM estimator. The robust sandwich VCE is
#   V = (G'WG)⁻¹ · G'W S W G · (G'WG)⁻¹,
# where G = −(μ.*Z)'X is the moment Jacobian and
# S = ((y−μ).*Z)'((y−μ).*Z) · n/(n−k) is the meat matrix.

dfg = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:,
    [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income, :firmsize]])
y_g = Float64.(dfg.docvis)
X_g = hcat(Float64.(dfg.private),  Float64.(dfg.chronic),
           Float64.(dfg.female),   Float64.(dfg.income),
           ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfg)))
Z_g = hcat(Float64.(dfg.firmsize), Float64.(dfg.chronic),
           Float64.(dfg.female),   Float64.(dfg.income),
           ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfg)))
n_g, k_g = size(X_g)
W_g = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(Z_g' * Z_g)))

function pgmm_Q(β, X, Z, y, W)
    h = Z' * (y .- exp.(X * β))
    return (h' * W * h)::Float64
end
function pgmm_grad!(g, β, X, Z, y, W)
    μ = exp.(X * β)
    h = Z' * (y .- μ)
    G = -(μ .* Z)' * X
    g .= 2 .* (G' * W * h)         # ∂Q/∂β = 2·G'Wh
end
function pgmm_hess!(H, β, X, Z, y, W)
    μ = exp.(X * β)
    G = -(μ .* Z)' * X
    H .= 2 .* (G' * W * G)         # Gauss–Newton-style Hessian
end

res_gmm = _optimize_compat(β -> pgmm_Q(β, X_g, Z_g, y_g, W_g),
                         (g, β) -> pgmm_grad!(g, β, X_g, Z_g, y_g, W_g),
                         (H, β) -> pgmm_hess!(H, β, X_g, Z_g, y_g, W_g),
                         zeros(k_g), Optim.NewtonTrustRegion())
b_gmm = Optim.minimizer(res_gmm)

# Robust sandwich VCE with the n/(n−k) finite-sample correction
μ_g  = exp.(X_g * b_gmm)
G_g  = -(μ_g .* Z_g)' * X_g
Shat = ((y_g .- μ_g) .* Z_g)' * ((y_g .- μ_g) .* Z_g) * (n_g / (n_g - k_g))
GtWG = G_g' * W_g * G_g
Vb   = LinearAlgebra.inv(GtWG) * G_g' * W_g * Shat * W_g * G_g *
       LinearAlgebra.inv(GtWG)
seb  = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(Vb))

# Mata-style display: `b \ seb` as a 2×5 matrix
println(":   b \\ seb")
mata_matrix_print(vcat(b_gmm', seb'))
```
